newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland moves to privatise Weglokoks coal trader.
newsitem.headline: Poland moves to privatise Weglokoks coal trader.

text.p: Poland's industry ministry has picked a consortium of foreign and domestic consulting agencies and banks to advise it in the privatisation of its coal trading company Weglokoks SA, the ministry said on Monday.

It said in a statement the consortium, due to prepare Weglokoks's privatisation strategy and oversee the sale of its shares, grouped Business Management and Finance SA consultancy, BGZ SA bank, Potworowski, Kinast, the legal firm Grant Thornton and PBR SA bank. @
Weglokoks's deputy president Stanislaw Zajac told Reuters a stake in his firm was likely to be offered to a strategic investor next year and a public share issue would then follow.
He said the company netted 18.9 million zlotys on 2.7 billion zloty sales in 1995.

Weglokoks, a virtual monopoly in coal trade before the 1989 fall of communism, sold 23 million tonnes of hard coal abroad last year and, according to a survey by the Polityka daily, was Poland's largest exporter.
